selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: At nightfall, what kind of condition is the human spirit described as being in?
questions.answer: It is described as weak, needy, and surrounded by many troubles and unknown things ahead.

questions.question: What problem does the worshipper face when he thinks about the future?
questions.answer: He feels surrounded by darkness, uncertainty, and many troubling events.

questions.question: What does the worshipper ask Allah to send into his world and future?
questions.answer: He asks for mercy and guidance that bring light and comfort.

questions.question: What does sleep remind the reader of in this passage?
questions.answer: It reminds the reader of death.

questions.question: How does the passage show honesty in worship?
questions.answer: It shows the worshipper openly admitting his sadness, fear, and need before Allah.

questions.question: What does it mean that Allah takes the place of mortal loved ones in prayer?
questions.answer: It means the heart turns to the One Who never leaves instead of depending only on people who cannot stay forever.

questions.question: In prayer, who protects a person from harmful things he fears?
questions.answer: Allah, the All-Compassionate Protector, protects him.

questions.question: What does the opening chapter of the prayer teach about who deserves praise?
questions.answer: It teaches that true and complete praise belongs to Allah alone.

questions.question: How can a small and lonely person become honored in worship?
questions.answer: By being connected to Allah, Who rules over all times and all things.

questions.question: What does the person ask for when saying, “Guide us to the Straight Path”?
questions.answer: He asks Allah to lead him on the path that brings everlasting happiness.

questions.question: What time of day is the passage mainly about?
questions.answer: It is about the night prayer at nightfall.

questions.question: What does the worshipper decide about things that disappear?
questions.answer: He decides not to give his heart to things that fade away.

questions.question: What kind of Being does the worshipper turn to instead?
questions.answer: He turns to Allah, the One Who remains forever.

questions.question: What does the passage say man does for a while about the unseen world?
questions.answer: It says he stops thinking about it for a time and pours out his grief before Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say a person does no matter what happens before going to sleep?
questions.answer: He performs his final act of worship.

questions.question: What is meant by ending the day’s record well?
questions.answer: It means closing the day with obedience and worship instead of neglect.

questions.question: Why should people not give deep praise to created beings as if they deserve it fully?
questions.answer: Because they are limited and needy, so they are not worthy of the kind of perfect praise that belongs to Allah.

questions.question: Why does the person begin with al-Fatiha instead of praising created beings?
questions.answer: Because created beings are not complete and do not deserve that highest praise.

questions.question: Why does the passage say the worshipper speaks in the name of all creatures?
questions.answer: Because the prayer expresses worship and need that fit the whole created world.

questions.question: What is the final request mentioned in the passage, and why is it important?
questions.answer: The final request is for guidance to the Straight Path, and it is important because it leads to everlasting success.

questions.question: What feelings or weaknesses make the night prayer especially important in this passage?
questions.answer: Human weakness, neediness, fear, sadness, and uncertainty make it especially important.

questions.question: During the night prayer, from whom does a person seek safety and shelter?
questions.answer: A person seeks refuge with Allah, the One Who lives forever and never fades.

questions.question: Why is turning to Allah at night especially fitting in this passage?
questions.answer: Because night reminds a person of weakness, loneliness, and need for protection.

questions.question: What is one reason a person stands to pray before sleeping?
questions.answer: He wants to end the record of his day in a good way.
